title: Check a transcript against the voice heard
statement: Never take a speech transcript as proof the learner spoke: check it against how much voice the recording held, since a recogniser can invent answers from silence.
example: In one build, one second of silence occasionally produced a plausible-looking answer the child had never said.
detail: A Grade 3 reading build found that one second of silence was occasionally producing a plausible-looking answer the child had never said. It made two independent fixes on 2026-07-30: the transcriber is now told to return nothing when it hears nothing, and, because an instruction is not a guarantee, the player measures how much of the recording held a voice and refuses words that could not have been spoken in that much time. A silent clip is never sent at all.
against: Accuracy on real children is unmeasured: the word error rate baseline is 1.2% on a synthetic-proxy corpus, and real child recordings are still unmeasured (grade3-reading/artifacts/judgment-corpus/distilled-src/07-SCORING-FEEDBACK-XP.md, line 191).

evidence.quote: One second of silence was occasionally producing a plausible-looking answer the child had never said.
the transcriber is now instructed to return nothing when it hears nothing
the player itself measures how much of the recording actually contained a voice and refuses to accept words that could not have been spoken in that much time.
